title: A tensor component is obtained from component rings of the factors
statement: For a ring $T$ and a connected component $Z$ of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], write $T_Z=T/I_Z$, where $I_Z$ is generated by the idempotents $e$ such that $Z\subseteq V(e)$; this is the component ring. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $B_1,B_2$ commutative $A$-algebras. For any connected component $Z$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(B_1\otimes_A B_2)$, there are connected components $Z_j$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ such that each projection maps $Z$ into $Z_j$. Put $D_j=(B_j)_{Z_j}$, $C=(B_1\otimes_A B_2)_Z$ and $E=D_1\otimes_A D_2$. The quotient $B_1\otimes_A B_2\to C$ factors through the canonical surjection $B_1\otimes_A B_2\to E$. The induced surjection $E\to C$ identifies $C$ with a component ring of $E$, compatibly with the maps from both $B_j$ and $D_j$.

source.place: Tag 00EG (lemma-connected-component), applied to both projections and to the idempotent quotient of the tensor product. This supplies the component reduction implicit in Hübner–Schmidt Theorem 6.4, printed p. 13.

proof.text: First check the hypotheses for applying the clopen-intersection theorem to affine spectra. For each ring $R$ used below, $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. Its covering by the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has quasi-compact pairwise intersection (the whole space); clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] therefore makes it quasi-separated as a scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. In particular its underlying space has all three hypotheses of the clopen-intersection theorem, with no Noetherian or local-connectedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 094L (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral), with Algebra Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact) and Schemes Tag 01KO (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated).

proof.text: Put $T=B_1\otimes_A B_2$ and $I=I_Z$. Choose $z\in Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasicompact-components-clopen-intersection], $Z$ is the intersection of the clopen neighbourhoods of $z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}T$. A clopen containing $z$ contains all of $Z$, since its intersection and its complement would otherwise separate $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], every such clopen is $D(u)=V(1-u)$ for an idempotent $u$. Thus the intersection is precisely $\bigcap_{e^2=e,\ Z\subseteq V(e)}V(e)=V(I)$: containing all the generators is equivalent to containing their ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], the quotient $p:T\twoheadrightarrow C=T/I$ identifies $\operatorname{Spec}C$ homeomorphically with $Z$. In particular this spectrum is nonempty and connected.

source.place: Tag 00EG (lemma-connected-component), proof; inputs Topology Tag 005F (lemma-connected-component-intersection), Algebra Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) and Tag 00E5 (lemma-spec-closed).

proof.text: Let $\iota_j:B_j\to T$ be the canonical tensor maps, and $\pi_j=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_j)$ their continuous spectrum maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The image $\pi_j(Z)$ is nonempty and connected: a separation by relatively open subsets would pull back to a separation of $Z$. Let $Z_j$ be the connected component containing $\pi_j(z)$. The union of $Z_j$ and the connected set $\pi_j(Z)$, which meet at $\pi_j(z)$, is connected (any separation would separate one of the two meeting sets). Maximality of $Z_j$ gives $\pi_j(Z)\subseteq Z_j$. This proves the required assertion about both projections.

source.place: Tag 00E2 (lemma-spec-functorial); elementary connected-image and maximal-connected-subset arguments for the two projections in the component reduction.

proof.text: Write $I_j=I_{Z_j}$, $q_j:B_j\twoheadrightarrow D_j=B_j/I_j$ and $E=D_1\otimes_A D_2$. For each generating idempotent $e\in I_j$ vanishing on $Z_j$, $\iota_j(e)$ is an idempotent vanishing on $Z$, since $\pi_j(Z)\subseteq Z_j$. Hence $\iota_j(e)\in I$, so $p\iota_j$ kills $I_j$ and induces an $A$-algebra map $f_j:D_j\to C$, $f_j(q_j(b))=p(\iota_j(b))$. The two maps have the same restriction from $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] to obtain $r:E\to C$ with $r(d_1\otimes d_2)=f_1(d_1)f_2(d_2)$ and the canonical map $q:T\to E$ with $q(b_1\otimes b_2)=q_1(b_1)\otimes q_2(b_2)$. Their composite agrees with $p$ on both factor maps, so uniqueness in that same node gives $rq=p$. The map $q$ is surjective: express an element of $E$ as a finite sum of pure tensors and lift each tensor factor through $q_1,q_2$. Since $p$ is surjective and $rq=p$, $r$ is surjective too.

source.place: Tag 00EG, component-ideal calculation for the projections; the algebra tensor pushout property is recorded in the cited Mathlib leaf, also used in Schemes Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: Let $K=\ker r$. Because $q$ is surjective and $rq=p$, we have $K=q(I)$ as ideals: an element $q(t)$ belongs to $K$ exactly when $p(t)=0$, that is $t\in I$. More explicitly, applying $q$ to a finite expression in the idempotent generators of $I$ shows that every element of $K$ is a linear combination over $E$ of their images, and each such image lies in $K$. Consequently $K$ is generated by the idempotents $q(e)$ with $e^2=e$ and $Z\subseteq V(e)$. This uses no assertion that arbitrary idempotents lift through $q$.

source.place: Elementary kernel and generated-ideal calculation in the idempotent-quotient reduction of Tag 00EG.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] to $q$ and $r$. Write $h=\operatorname{Spec}q$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}r(\operatorname{Spec}C)=V(K)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}E$. These maps identify $\operatorname{Spec}C$ homeomorphically with $W$ and $\operatorname{Spec}E$ with a subspace of $\operatorname{Spec}T$; since $rq=p$, $h$ takes $W$ bijectively onto $Z$. Thus $W$ is nonempty and connected. If a connected subset $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}E$ contains $W$, its continuous image $h(U)$ is connected and contains $Z$. Maximality of $Z$ forces $h(U)=Z=h(W)$; injectivity of $h$ forces $U=W$. Therefore $W$ is a connected component of $\operatorname{Spec}E$. The connected-image argument is the elementary separation argument of step 3.

source.place: Tag 00E5 (lemma-spec-closed), applied to both surjections; maximality of a connected component under the resulting subspace identification.

proof.text: It remains to identify the ring, rather than only its spectrum. Let $I_W\subseteq E$ be generated by all idempotents $a\in E$ with $W\subseteq V(a)$. Every idempotent generator of $K$ in step 5 vanishes on $W=V(K)$; hence $K\subseteq I_W$. Conversely, if $a^2=a$ and $W\subseteq V(a)$, then $r(a)$ belongs to every prime ideal of $C$, by the spectrum identification in step 6. Thus $D(r(a))=\varnothing=D(0)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] implies $r(a)=0$, because both $r(a)$ and $0$ are idempotents with this same basic open. Every generator of $I_W$ therefore lies in $K$, giving $I_W=K$. The surjection $r$ induces $E/I_W\cong C$: the inverse sends $c$ to the class of any lift $d\in E$ with $r(d)=c$, which is independent of the lift since their difference lies in $K=I_W$. Its composites with the maps $D_j\to E/I_W$ are $f_j$, by the formula for $r$ in step 4; composing with $q_j$ gives $p\iota_j$. These are exactly the required compatibilities with $D_j$ and $B_j$. If $T=0$ there is no connected component $Z$, so the original assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition), uniqueness; comparison of the idempotent-generated ideals in the component reduction of Tag 00EG.

proof_origin.place: Explicit two-factor component reduction, using Tag 00EG and its cited component/clopen route (Topology 005F, Algebra 00EE), quotient spectra 00E5, and the tensor-product universal property. No appeal to Hübner–Schmidt Theorem 6.4 is needed for this elementary ring-theoretic input.

lean.statement: theorem tensor_component_from_factor_components (A : Type u) (B₁ : Type v) (B₂ : Type w) [CommRing A] [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂] [Algebra A B₁] [Algebra A B₂] (z : PrimeSpectrum (B₁ ⊗[A] B₂)) : ∃ (z₁ : PrimeSpectrum B₁) (z₂ : PrimeSpectrum B₂), (PrimeSpectrum.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : B₁ →ₐ[A] B₁ ⊗[A] B₂).toRingHom) '' connectedComponent z ⊆ connectedComponent z₁ ∧ (PrimeSpectrum.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B₂ →ₐ[A] B₁ ⊗[A] B₂).toRingHom) '' connectedComponent z ⊆ connectedComponent z₂ ∧ Function.Surjective (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A (componentIdeal B₁ z₁)) (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A (componentIdeal B₂ z₂))) ∧ ∃ r : ((B₁ ⧸ componentIdeal B₁ z₁) ⊗[A] (B₂ ⧸ componentIdeal B₂ z₂)) →ₐ[A] ((B₁ ⊗[A] B₂) ⧸ componentIdeal (B₁ ⊗[A] B₂) z), Function.Surjective r ∧ r.comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A (componentIdeal B₁ z₁)) (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A (componentIdeal B₂ z₂))) = Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A (componentIdeal (B₁ ⊗[A] B₂) z) ∧ ∃ (y : PrimeSpectrum ((B₁ ⧸ componentIdeal B₁ z₁) ⊗[A] (B₂ ⧸ componentIdeal B₂ z₂))) (e : (((B₁ ⧸ componentIdeal B₁ z₁) ⊗[A] (B₂ ⧸ componentIdeal B₂ z₂)) ⧸ componentIdeal ((B₁ ⧸ componentIdeal B₁ z₁) ⊗[A] (B₂ ⧸ componentIdeal B₂ z₂)) y) ≃ₐ[A] ((B₁ ⊗[A] B₂) ⧸ componentIdeal (B₁ ⊗[A] B₂) z)), e.toAlgHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A (componentIdeal ((B₁ ⧸ componentIdeal B₁ z₁) ⊗[A] (B₂ ⧸ componentIdeal B₂ z₂)) y)) = r
